facts: Visual object tracking is considered as a numerical optimization problem.
During normal tracking conditions when the object is visible from frame to frame, local optimization is used.
Local optimization is used to track the local mode of the similarity measure.
The parameter space includes translation, rotation and scale.
Local tracking is prone to failure when the object becomes partially or totally occluded.
Object detection is considered as a global optimization problem.
Object detection is solved via Adaptive Simulated Annealing (ASA).
Adaptive Simulated Annealing (ASA) avoids becoming trapped at local modes.
Adaptive Simulated Annealing (ASA) is much faster than exhaustive search.
Adaptive Simulated Annealing (ASA) stochastically samples the parameter space.
Cluster analysis is applied on the sampled parameter space to redetect the object.
Cluster analysis is applied to renew the local tracker.
A numerical hybrid local and global mode-seeking tracker is validated on challenging airborne videos with heavy occlusion and large camera motions.
An approach outperforms state-of-the-art trackers on the VIVID benchmark datasets.
